themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked 700% THIS WEEK to 5 complaints vs. a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either a sudden proliferation of unlicensed or non-compliant vendors or a coordinated enforcement crackdown that is generating resident friction.
evidence: 5 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 6.29)
Highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating sudden and significant shift in resident behavior or vendor activity
Spike is recent enough to warrant real-time investigation before trend stabilizes
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food carts flooding Parkchester/Soundview this week? Interview Health Dept. and local merchants.
Is this spike tied to seasonal vendors or a specific event? Check Unionport Road or park corridors for vendor clusters.

themes_detail.label: Maintenance and Facility Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints jumped 300% THIS WEEK to 10 complaints vs. a 2.5 weekly average, a significant spike suggesting deterioration or neglect of public or private facilities that warrants rapid investigation.
evidence: 10 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score: 3.44)
Second-most recent spike in dataset, indicates emerging facility crisis
Aligns with CB budget request patterns: repeated demands for park building upgrades, library renovation, senior center upgrades suggest chronic facility neglect
reporting_angles: Which public facilities are deteriorating? Map the 10 complaints to specific parks, libraries, or senior centers.
Interview CB District 209 about whether this spike reflects long-standing facility neglect or a new failure event.

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis Ending
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints plummeted 79% THIS WEEK to 42 complaints vs. a 198.5 weekly average, a dramatic drop that either signals the end of a seasonal heating crisis or the temporary resolution of widespread building system failures.
evidence: 42 heat/hot water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 198.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (79% drop, z-score: -3.25)
Heat/hot water remains the second-largest complaint category overall (2,335 complaints over 90 days), but dramatic weekly drop suggests resolution or seasonal shift
Timing suggests either spring-induced reduced heating demand or emergency repairs completed this week
reporting_angles: Did the city complete emergency heat repairs in Parkchester/Soundview this week? Check HPD enforcement records.
Is this drop seasonal (spring warmth reducing demand) or crisis-driven (emergency repairs)? Interview residents in buildings that filed complaints.

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Complaints Elevated
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints spiked 114% three weeks ago to 15 complaints vs. a 7.0 weekly average, a sustained elevation that may indicate persistent street racing, illegally modified vehicles, or construction equipment activity.
evidence: 15 vehicle noise complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 7.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (114% spike, z-score: 4.62)
Spike occurred 3 weeks ago, so may have already resolved or may be ongoing—requires follow-up data to confirm if persistent
Vehicle noise is distinct signal from broader residential noise (which is DOWN 30% this week), suggesting targeted street-level problem
reporting_angles: Is there a street racing or illegal modified vehicle problem on specific corridors? Check with NYPD Precinct 43 for enforcement data.
Map the 15 complaints by location to identify hotspot areas (highway corridors, major avenues) for targeted reporting.

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints surged 400% last week to 5 complaints vs. a 1.0 weekly average, suggesting residents are frustrated with a specific city enforcement action or traffic enforcement initiative.
evidence: 5 real-time enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (400% spike, z-score: 4.62)
Complaints category is vague; requires investigation to determine what enforcement action triggered resident complaints
May be related to parking enforcement, traffic cameras, or quality-of-life policing initiatives
reporting_angles: What specific enforcement action prompted this spike? File FOIL request for NYPD real-time enforcement deployment records.
Interview residents who filed complaints to understand their grievances with enforcement tactics.
